item.title: Visit to Papua New Guinea for Golden Jubilee
item.content:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will travel to Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea from 15 to 17 September to commemorate the 50th Anniversary of Papua New Guinea’s independence.

Australia is proud to participate in this milestone celebration.

Papua New Guinea is not only one of our closest neighbours but also the truest of friends.

Our unique relationship has been forged by shared history, mutual respect and ongoing collaboration.

Australia’s partnership with Papua New Guinea is comprehensive and includes support for health, security, education, infrastructure, development, gender equality, sport and agriculture.

In addition to the anniversary celebrations, Prime Minister Albanese will meet with the Prime Minister of Papua New Guinea, the Honourable James Marape MP.

Prime Minister Albanese will be joined in Port Moresby by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence, the Hon Richard Marles MP, and Minister for Pacific Island Affairs the Hon Pat Conroy MP.

Quotes attributable to Prime Minister Albanese:

“I am honoured to be involved in this momentous occasion, celebrating Papua New Guinea’s Golden Jubilee.

“Ties between our nations run deep, and over the past 50 years our friendship has continued to evolve and mature.

“Australia and Papua New Guinea have a special relationship based on shared values, and a vision for a stable and prosperous Pacific region.

“I look forward to discussions with Prime Minister Marape on how we can continue to expand our relationship as neighbours, partners and equals.”
